Ishi
ISH-eye
n. (proper, several men of Judah and Simeon; Hebrew, my salvation)
Hebrew Yishiy, from yesha, salvation — my salvation, or saving. A separate Hebrew word spelled the same way in English, iyshiy, means my husband, and is the word God promises Israel shall call him in Hosea 2:16.

Biblical Definition

The name belongs to at least three men in the registers of Judah and Simeon. “And the sons of Appaim; Ishi. And the sons of Ishi; Sheshan. And the children of Sheshan; Ahlai” (1 Chronicles 2:31) — a line that continues through a daughter married to an Egyptian servant, because Sheshan had no sons. “And the sons of Ishi were, Zoheth, and Benzoheth” (1 Chronicles 4:20). And he is the father of the four captains who took mount Seir: “having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi” (1 Chronicles 4:42). The English spelling collides with a different Hebrew word in one of the tenderest verses in the prophets: “And it shall be at that day, saith the LORD, that thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali” (Hosea 2:16) — my husband, and no longer my master.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as the name of men in the registers of Judah and Simeon, and separately as the Hebrew word rendered my husband in Hosea 2:16.

expand to see more

SALVATION, n. The redemption of man from the bondage of sin and liability to eternal death, by the atonement of Christ.

HUSBAND, n. A man contracted or joined to a woman by marriage; a correlative term to wife.

MASTER, n. A director; a governor; one who rules or directs; a lord or owner.

BAAL, n. The chief male deity of the Phoenicians and Canaanites; a name signifying lord or master.

BETROTH, v.t. To contract to any one, in order to a future marriage; to affiance.

Key Scripture

1 Chronicles 2:31 — "And the sons of Appaim; Ishi. And the sons of Ishi; Sheshan. And the children of Sheshan; Ahlai."

1 Chronicles 4:20 — "And the sons of Shimon were, Amnon, and Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. And the sons of Ishi were, Zoheth, and Benzoheth."

1 Chronicles 4:42 — "And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi."

Hosea 2:16 — "And it shall be at that day, saith the LORD, that thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali."

Modern Corruption

God is related to either as a distant master to be placated or as a companion with no authority; Hosea 2:16 promises a people who will call him Ishi, my husband, and no more Baali, my master.

expand to see more

Hosea 2:16 is a single verse that corrects two opposite errors at once. To a nation that had been calling God Baali — my master, in a word indistinguishable from the name of the idol they had been worshipping — God promises a day when they will call him Ishi, my husband. Servile religion, which deals with God as a proprietor to be kept satisfied, is not what he is after; he is after a covenant of affection, and the verses around it use the language of betrothal: I will betroth thee unto me for ever, in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.

The safeguard against sentimentality is in the same chapter, which is one of the most severe in the prophets — a wife pursued after her lovers, hedged up with thorns, stripped and left in the wilderness, and only then allured and spoken to comfortably. The intimacy promised is on the far side of judgment, not instead of it. And the change is in the name a people use for God, which is always a good measure of what they actually believe about him. The registers of Chronicles carry the same three letters as a plain personal name: my salvation.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yishiy (H3469), my salvation; yesha (H3468), salvation; iysh (H376), a man or husband; Baal (H1180), my master.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yishiy (H3469) — Ishi; my salvation, a personal name in Judah and Simeon.

Hebrew yesha (H3468) — salvation, deliverance; the root of the personal name.

Hebrew iyshiy — my husband, from iysh, a man; the word of Hosea 2:16.

Hebrew Baaliy (H1180) — my master; the name God says they shall use no more.

Hebrew aras (H781) — to betroth; I will betroth thee unto me for ever.

Usage

"“And the sons of Ishi; Sheshan” — a line kept through a daughter."

"“The sons of Ishi” — four captains who took mount Seir."

"“Thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali”."
